motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda with the following amendments : 1. Item 13.B., Section 6 (Use of Sponsorship Funds ) remove the provisions beginning with “purchase and maintain” through “cover administrative” and to add “other one-time use of funds approved by the City Council.” 2. Item 13 .B., updat e Appendix A Fee Schedule to reflect fee schedule presented in the Work Session. 3. Item 13 .F., update the Scope of Work to include a kickoff meeting noticed for the full City Council and emphasize Councilmember involvement throughout the process. 4. Item 14 .A., Section 2.45.040 (Limitations of the Youth City Council Authority ): update the numbering of items 1-4 and revise Item 1 to read “The youth city council must have a quorum in order to conduct business. A quorum is one more than half of the youth city council voting members or at least five voting members, whichever is less. ” Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent items approved with changes
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after narrowing how sponsorship money may be spent, updating the city fee schedule, and setting a Youth City Council quorum.
motions.impact: Mostly housekeeping. The one piece that could reach you is the updated fee schedule, but the motion doesn't say which fees changed or by how much.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approv ing the Third Amendment to the 2025 -2026 Fiscal Year Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to a dopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approv ing the Third Amendment to the 2025 -2026 Fiscal Year Annual Budget. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Third change to this year's city budget
motions.summary: The council approved a third amendment to the 2025-2026 budget, adjusting the city's spending plan for the fiscal year now ending.
motions.impact: The motion doesn't say what was moved or added, so no change to your bills or services is stated — this is the city squaring its books before the year closes.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2 026-2027 Interim Budget and the Proposed Certified Tax Rate; and Discontinuing DebtBook Services
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2 026-2027 Interim Budget and the Proposed Certified Tax Rate; and Discontinuing DebtBook Services. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Interim budget and proposed tax rate adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted an interim budget for the 2026-2027 fiscal year and the proposed certified tax rate, and dropped the city's DebtBook software service.
motions.impact: This keeps the city funded until a final budget is adopted and sets the property tax rate the city is proposing. The motion states no dollar figures.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.15 Concept Plans adding condition that council be notified every time a concept plan will be presented to Planning Commission
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to a dopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.15 Concept Plans adding condition that council be notified every time a concept plan will be presented to Planning Commission . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Council must be told when concept plans go forward
motions.summary: The city changed its development rules so the council is notified every time a concept plan is set to go before the Planning Commission.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day for residents. Council members simply get advance notice of proposed developments before the Planning Commission reviews them.
